sentence: Female infant who was admitted at 7 months of age due to a brief generalized tonic-clonic seizure, without an infectious process or associated fever, which was repeated with similar characteristics 23 hours after the first episode, while she was admitted.
No focal onset of the crisis was observed, with maintained vital signs and a normal subsequent physical and neurological examination.
The parents did not report any personal history of note, she attended periodic health check-ups and her psychomotor and height-weight development followed a normal course.
Upon her admission, a complete blood count, kidney and liver function tests, acute phase reactants, brain ultrasound and electroencephalogram were performed, with normal results.
Given the observation of a conflictive socio-familial situation, a search for toxic substances was carried out in urine, which turned out to be positive for cocaine in two successive samples.

The first sample showed a quantified level of cocaine metabolites in urine of 1.7 µg/ml and the second, collected a few hours later, 0.4 µg/ml (our laboratory's cut-off point of 0.3 µg/ml) , which became negative 48 hours after admission.

The father is a habitual cannabis smoker, but the relatives denied the consumption of cocaine at home or in their close socio-familial environment and pointed out the possibility of contact with environmental smoke in a closed place where they were hours before the start of the crisis.
Under surveillance by the social worker assigned since discharge, the patient has not had seizures again in the following six months and her psychomotor development follows a normal course.
